items.name: Behaviour
items.doc: Base class of gameplay scripts. Export a subclass as the default export of a module in scripts/ and attach it with the Script component. Class fields are defaults overridable from Script.props.

members.doc: The owning entity.
false skips update callbacks.

Default false. While time.scale is 0 (game.paused) the engine calls onUpdate and onLateUpdate only on behaviours whose runWhilePaused is true, with the REAL frame time as dt (time.dt is 0 then; time.unscaledDt is the real one). Set it as a class field (`runWhilePaused = true;`) on pause menus and anything else that must react while gameplay is frozen. onFixedUpdate never runs while paused. ui events and world.on listeners are delivered either way.

members.sig: shapeCast(shape: CastShape3D, from: Vec3 | { x: number; y: number; z: number } | readonly [number, number, number], to: Vec3Like, opts?: RaycastOptions): RayHit<Vec3> | null
members.doc: Sweeps a sphere or box from `from` to `to` (3D, when `from` has a z) and returns the first collider it touches: distance is how far the centre travels, point the contact point, normal the hit surface's normal (pointing back at the shape). Colliders the shape already overlaps at `from` are skipped, like a ray that starts inside one; a collider it only touches blocks the cast only if the shape moves towards it. Answers 'will this fit / how far can it go' for shapes where a ray is too thin. Same options as raycast; from a behaviour pass { ignore: this.entity }.

members.sig: shapeCast(shape: CastShape2D, from: Vec2Like, to: Vec2Like, opts?: RaycastOptions): RayHit<Vec2> | null
members.doc: Sweeps a circle or box from `from` to `to` (2D) and returns the first collider it touches: distance is how far the centre travels, point the contact point, normal the hit surface's normal (pointing back at the shape). Colliders the shape already overlaps at `from` are skipped, like a ray that starts inside one; a collider it only touches blocks the cast only if the shape moves towards it. Example: physics.shapeCast({ shape: "box", size: [16, 24] }, vec2(x, y), vec2(x, y - 40), { ignore: this.entity }). Throws an Error that explains the fix when the shape is wrong (misspelt name, "sphere" in 2D, missing size).

items.name: RngAPI
items.doc: Deterministic random numbers (seeded per run). Math.random is routed here too.

members.doc: Inclusive.

Reseeds the deterministic world RNG (use from tools/tests for seed -> level determinism). The running game draws from this one RNG, so reseeding it changes the game's random sequence: a level generator should use rng.create(seed) instead.

Creates an independent, deterministic generator with the same methods as rng. It has its own state and never reads or changes the world RNG (or Math.random), so a tool can generate a level from a seed without disturbing the running game. Algorithm: mulberry32 (32-bit state, one step per draw). The algorithm and the draws each method consumes are STABLE across engine versions, so a stored seed keeps giving the same sequence. The seed is reduced to 32 bits (ToUint32: integer part, modulo 2^32); 0 is a valid seed. Throws for a non-number or non-finite seed. Example: const r = rng.create(7); r.int(1, 6).

items.name: Rng
items.doc: An independent seeded generator from rng.create(seed). Algorithm mulberry32, stable across engine versions: the same seed gives the same sequence on every platform. Every method draws a fixed number of 32-bit steps (float, range, int and chance: one per call; pick: one, none for an empty array; shuffle: items.length - 1), so a sequence does not depend on the arguments.

members.doc: Next number in [0, 1): a 32-bit step divided by 2^32.
min + (max - min) * float(); in [min, max).
Integer in [min, max], both inclusive (arguments are truncated to integers): min + floor(float() * (max - min + 1)). Returns min when max <= min (still one draw).
True with probability p (default 0.5): float() < p.
A random item (items[floor(float() * length)]), or undefined for an empty array.
A shuffled copy (Fisher-Yates from the end, j = floor(float() * (i + 1))); the input is not modified.
Restarts this generator from seed n (same reduction as rng.create); the same as a new rng.create(n). Does not touch the world RNG.

members.sig: measureText(text: string, opts?: { fontSize?: number; font?: string; maxWidth?: number }): { width: number; height: number }
members.doc: Size of `text` laid out like Text rendering (wraps at maxWidth > 0). Headless runs approximate 0.6 * fontSize per character (with a warning).

members.sig: textureSize(path: string): { width: number; height: number }
members.doc: Pixel size of the texture file at the project-relative `path`, e.g. assets.textureSize("assets/hero.png"). This is the size a Sprite without `size` or `region` is drawn at and that entity.bounds() uses. A missing or unreadable file gives 32 x 32, the size of the missing-texture checker. Cached per file and modification time, so it is cheap to call every frame. Works headless (it reads the file, not the GPU texture). Throws for an empty or non-string path.
